title: Read-then-write race: two gateways both allow the 5th request (limit 4)
caption: Fix: one atomic operation (INCR, or a short server-side script) that increments and returns the new value.

messages.label: GET count → 3
messages.note: Gateway 2 reads before gateway 1 writes back. It also sees 3.

messages.label: SET count = 4 (allow)
messages.note: Both allowed: 5 requests passed a limit of 4, and the counter says 4. The lost update grows with traffic.

scenarios.name: Fix: atomic INCR
scenarios.summary: One round trip that increments and returns the new value: each gateway sees a different number, so exactly one request is rejected.

messages.label: 4 → allow
messages.note: It gets 4: the last allowed slot.

messages.label: INCR count
messages.note: Gateway 2 increments at almost the same moment.
It gets 5, which is over the limit: rejected. No lost update is possible.

scenarios.name: Alternative: Lua script
scenarios.summary: For token buckets (read tokens, refill, take one) run the whole check as one server-side script so it is atomic too.

messages.label: EVAL take_token(key)
messages.note: The script reads tokens and last refill time, refills, decides and writes back, all inside the store.

messages.label: EVAL take_token(key)
messages.note: Scripts run one at a time on that key, so there is no interleaving.
